description: Replace the n1024 host-driven width-16 Householder panel sequence with a true width-64 two-stage reducer: batch-parallel exact compact-WY dense-to-band updates, cluster-distributed resident band storage, staggered multi-train bulge chasing, and tiled reflector replay. Preserve saved eigenvalues/WY geometric repair, exact certificates and fallbacks, all size routes and CUDA guards; use strict or compensated updates where certificate margins require them and profile each phase.

Implemented the first dense-only n1024 width-64 two-stage route with compact-WY dense-to-band panels, compact global band storage, a two-train 384-thread Householder bulge chase, eight-CTA fused tridiagonal solve, tiled scalar replay, and exact certification fallback while leaving every non-dense n1024 repair route unchanged. The extension built cleanly and kernelguard was clean, but validation reached the first n1024 case and CUDA rejected the width-64 panel_qr_wy launch: its inherited full-panel shared layout requires about 266 KB for the 960x64 leading panel, above the B200 per-block limit. No correctness metric was produced; the next trial moves the panel matrix out of shared memory while retaining width 64.

Completed the first full dense-only n1024 width-64 two-stage implementation after moving the three oversized leading panel QR matrices to their global V workspace. Compact-WY panels, compact 128-column band storage, a 384-thread staggered two-train Householder chase, eight-CTA fused tridiagonal solve, 32 one-warp replay tiles per matrix, one exact Newton/Rayleigh correction, and library fallback coexist with the unchanged saved-WY geometric/non-dense routes. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is 27815.552 us versus parent 23665.577; dense n1024 is 313840.220 us. Exact profile at b5ffe6b44 attributes 91.805 ms to scalar reflector replay, 49.539 ms to chase, 37.248 ms to panel QR, 3.535 ms to the fused tridiagonal solve, and also shows a whole-batch exact repair tail because high-precision tensor-core panel updates do not clear the certificate at n1024.

Split each width-64 dense-to-band similarity transform by keeping its left compact-WY update at high tensor-core precision and switching the right update to strict FP32, then restoring high precision for the bulge and reflector replay phases. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 313787.974 us versus 313840.220 and full geomean is 27797.400 us versus 27815.552, both effectively unchanged; the exact repair tail remains active, so one-sided strict panel arithmetic alone does not move this n1024 route into the certificate-clean basin.

Ran the entire n1024 dense-to-band similarity transform and reverse dense-reflector replay in strict FP32, retaining the same width-64 panels, two-train bulge stream, clustered tridiagonal solve, exact certificate and fallback. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Dense n1024 rises from 313787.974 to 318256.266 us and full geomean is 27828.743 us; the exact repair tail still remains. This brackets tensor-core transform arithmetic: full strictness costs about 4.47 ms and does not clear the certificate, localizing the unsafe result to the bulge/replay or reduced eigensolve rather than only the dense panel GEMMs.

Bypassed the final Newton/certificate repair for one raw-output diagnostic after full strict dense-panel and backtransform arithmetic still selected whole-batch fallback. Build and kernelguard pass, but the first dense n1024 validation matrix fails the eigen-equation gate with residual 3.86 versus 3.13 allowed (scaled 246). The reduced factors are therefore substantially inaccurate before correction; this failure localizes the problem to the bulge/replay or tridiagonal eigensolve rather than certificate bookkeeping. Restoring the known-good exact-fallback commit before the next structural edit.

Replaced the two-stage route's 25-step fused reduced eigensolve with the existing 32-step shifted inverse solver and a separate ordered width-16 reorthogonalization before reflector replay. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is 318650.441 us and full geomean 27856.670 us, so tighter eigenvalue localization and explicit reorthogonalization do not remove the repair tail. Exact profile at 5501a3798 measures solve 3.298 ms and reorth 0.468 ms while replay remains 92.266 ms, chase 49.547 ms, panel QR 37.222 ms, and exact sytrd repair is still present; the measured error therefore lies upstream/downstream of the reduced solve.

Replaced the two-train wavefront with the exact column-major serial width-64 Householder stream over the same compact global band. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass; dense n1024 residuals improve to scaled eigen/reconstruction/orthogonality 0.0182/0.0203/0.122 after the retained strict Newton/Rayleigh step, and the whole-batch cuSOLVER repair disappears. Dense n1024 is 349310.201 us and full geomean 28030.028 us. Exact profile at 9997e4453 shows no sytrd repair: serial chase costs 151.427 ms, tiled scalar replay 127.290 ms, panel QR 37.190 ms, solve/reorth 3.295/0.458 ms. This measures the correctness cost of the prior overlap and leaves dependency-safe chase concurrency plus lower-traffic replay as concrete openings.

Reworked the exact serial route's reverse replay into two-warp 64-eigenvector tiles: each CTA loads one width-64 reflector into shared memory once and reuses it across all 64 columns, retaining bitwise reflector order and the certificate-clean serial chase. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass with unchanged dense n1024 residuals. Dense n1024 improves 349310.201->330634.369 us and full geomean 28030.028->27912.008 us, measuring an 18.676 ms gain from lower reflector-stream traffic and fewer replay CTAs.

Expanded shared reflector replay from two warps/64 eigenvectors/960 CTAs to four warps/128 eigenvectors/480 CTAs while preserving exact arithmetic and certificate-clean serial chase. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass with unchanged target residuals. Dense n1024 regresses 330634.369->334894.908 us; the lower reflector traffic does not offset reduced replay scheduling headroom. Full geomean is 27870.757 us, with unrelated mixed n1024 variance accounting for the apparent aggregate improvement.

Implemented a four-CTA-per-matrix cluster-resident width-64 chase: each rank holds 256 rows of the compact band in 128 KB shared memory, exact serial reflectors use DSM, and symmetric rank-2 elements are distributed across 1024 cluster threads; also restored the measured two-warp replay. The extension builds, kernelguard is clean, and all 39 validation cases pass at batch 4 with scaled dense n1024 residuals 0.0186/0.0213/0.127. The active batch-60 benchmark aborts during the clustered n1024 route with CUDA unspecified launch failure before producing a metric, so the full-grid resource/lifetime issue must be fixed before timing this design.

Bounded the four-CTA cluster-resident chase to five 12-matrix launches, fixing the full-grid CUDA launch failure while restoring the measured two-warp replay. Kernelguard and all 39 validations pass with dense n1024 residuals 0.0186/0.0213/0.127. Dense n1024 is 896288.025 us and full geomean 30146.804 us. Exact profile at cb0088dc6 shows five clustered chases total 716.356 ms (143.271 ms each), shared replay 109.157 ms, panel QR 37.185 ms, solve/reorth 3.303/0.459 ms, and no exact repair. DSM plus per-reflector cluster synchronization gives no per-wave speedup over the 151.427 ms single-CTA global chase, while the conservative launch bound serializes five waves.

Raised the cluster-resident chase chunk from 12 to 36 matrices so each 144-CTA launch would fill one B200 SM wave. Build, kernelguard, and 39/39 validation still pass, but the active batch-60 benchmark again reports CUDA unspecified launch failure from the larger clustered launch and produces no metric. The stable launch bound lies below 36 matrices; the next bracket tests 24 matrices/96 CTAs while retaining exact DSM arithmetic.

Bracketed the cluster-resident chase at 24 matrices/96 CTAs per launch. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass, but the batch-60 active benchmark still reports CUDA unspecified launch failure before a metric. Together with the 36-matrix result and the stable 12-matrix point, this bounds the robust launch size below 24; testing 16 matrices/64 CTAs next.

Completed the cluster launch bracket at 16 matrices/64 CTAs. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass with unchanged certificate-clean residuals. The full active benchmark is stable: dense n1024 measures 752806.620 us and geomean 29750.586 us, improving the stable 12-matrix DSM point by 143.481 ms by reducing five chase waves to four, but remaining 422.172 ms slower than the global-band serial route with shared replay. Larger 24- and 36-matrix grids both failed at runtime, so this records the robust DSM occupancy boundary measured on B200.

Dense n1024 improves from the strict global route's 330634.369 to 324297.872 us and full geomean to 27891.393 us, recovering 6.336 ms while retaining no exact repair.

Dense n1024 improves 324297.872->305300.018 us and full geomean 27891.393->27734.496 us. Exact profile at 32919ba17 measures chase 132.361 ms versus 151.427 ms for the 192-thread serial point, replay 109.252 ms, panel QR 37.191 ms, and solve/reorth 3.299/0.463 ms, with no exact repair.

The extension builds and kernelguard is clean, but CUDA rejects the n1024 chase launch with invalid argument at the first validation case, consistent with the compiled kernel's per-block register/resource footprint exceeding the 768-thread launch geometry. No metric was produced; restoring the valid 384-thread commit before testing a bounded 512-thread point.

Retried the exact flattened chase at 512 threads after the 768-thread launch rejection. Build and kernelguard pass, but CUDA again rejects the n1024 chase launch with invalid argument before validation, bounding this kernel's compiled block-resource limit at the valid 384-thread geometry. No metric was produced; restoring the 384-thread commit.

Prefetched groups of eight consecutive bulge reflectors into shared memory and applied them in identical reverse order, reducing replay barriers eightfold while retaining the 64-column tile and exact arithmetic. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass with unchanged residuals, but dense n1024 regresses 305300.018->322594.462 us and full geomean to 27873.876 us. The larger shared working set and dynamically indexed eight-reflector inner loop cost more than the removed barriers; single-reflector shared replay remains the measured point.

Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Dense n1024 improves from the width-eight group's 322594.462 to 307390.633 us, but remains 2.091 ms slower than single-reflector shared replay at 305300.018 us; full geomean is 27773.477 us. The bracket shows grouped replay overhead persists even at the smallest useful group.

Restored the faster single-reflector shared replay. The four active update windows are non-overlapping and full validation passed 39/39 with unchanged dense n1024 residuals 6.01/7.32/5.60/0.57, but reducing per-reflector parallelism outweighed fewer scheduler levels: full metric regressed from 27585.770843 to 27822.476049 and dense n1024 from 282566.111 us to 318145.406 us.

The dense n1024 classifier now uses a true width-64 two-stage route: batch-parallel compact-WY dense-to-band panels (global-memory panels for the large leading blocks and shared panels for the tail), compact 128-float-pitch band storage, a dependency-safe two-train exact bulge chase, a 32-step tridiagonal solve plus clustered reorthogonalization, an eight-warp 1024x32 resident reflector replay, one Rayleigh/Newton refinement, and the existing certificate/fallback path. Non-dense n1024 cases, every other size route, and CUDA guards remain preserved. The key correctness result is that n1024 has up to sixteen reflector stages per column: the inherited interval-three scheduler tracked only two columns and silently dropped active stages; interval eight keeps the current and previous columns non-overlapping and removes exact repair. Final clean build and validation passed 39/39 with dense n1024 scaled eigen/reconstruction/diagonalization/orthogonality residuals 6.07/7.34/5.50/0.554. Final full metric is 27580.438373 (trial 24 best observed 27568.514083) versus parent 23665.577, and dense n1024 is 283063.489 us. Measured alternatives include exact serial chase 132.361 ms, four 96-thread trains at 318145 us total, DSM cluster chunks at 752807-896288 us total with larger chunks failing launch, grouped reflector replay slower than single replay, one/four/eight-warp resident replay scaling from 434673 to 312867 to 283043 us total, and flattened/warp-striped rank updates regressing chase to 159.562 ms / total 301057 us. Continue from this commit by attacking the two equal 109 ms phases: for chase, retain all active trains explicitly if testing interval-three scheduling (up to six, rather than dropping older columns) or distribute one matrix across CTAs with a launch-safe synchronization scheme; for replay, fuse adjacent-column reflectors within resident row windows to reduce the four barriers per reflector, because merely increasing resident warps has reached parity. The 37.2 ms panel phase is the next independent target, especially batched/fused global-panel QR. NCU on the final chase and replay should distinguish barrier issue stalls from shared-memory throughput before choosing the follow-up brief.
